planSections.title: TL;DR
paragraphs: Start with three existing Harbor adapters: GAIA validation, SpreadsheetBench Verified, and SWE-bench Verified, covering research, office work, and coding. Each contributes 1/3 of the index. Run six DashScope models once per release and retain model and SDK history.

GitHub Actions orchestrates Harbor ACP on one hosted runner per task. Build QwenPaw from the workflow’s current commit. Keep evaluation dependencies isolated, archive results on a dedicated data branch, and reuse website deployment. Parity, comparison, and attribution are offline.

planSections.title: Scope and leaderboards
paragraphs: GAIA validation: 165 tasks; SpreadsheetBench Verified: 400; SWE-bench Verified: 500. Domain leaderboards weight their benchmarks equally; individual boards use native scores. Overall ranking requires complete coverage.

Highlight the highest-scoring SDK result per model while retaining every historical point and table row. Revisit PawBench and ClawEval after public Harbor adapter and resource verification. Terminal-Bench and AppWorld are out of scope.

planSections.title: Model scope
paragraphs: Use the DashScope Beijing pay-as-you-go API throughout, with no implicit model switching. Start with six configurations:
Qwen: qwen3.8-max-0902, qwen3.8-27b; DeepSeek: deepseek-v4-pro-0813, deepseek-v4.1-flash; GLM: glm-5.3, glm-5.2.
Freeze model IDs, reasoning settings, tool policy, provider region, task hashes, source SHA, and pricing. Record dates and available model versions to account for provider updates behind the same ID.

planSections.title: Code and execution architecture
paragraphs: No root evaluation package. YAML lives in .github/bench, workflows in .github/workflows, helpers in scripts/bench, and the UI in website/src/pages/Evaluation. Pin Harbor and LiteLLM in an isolated uv environment.

Each model runs 1,065 tasks in nine batches of at most 128. Each task gets a matrix job; max-parallel is 8. Models and batches run sequentially, totaling 6,390 task-trials. Preserve native timeouts and reject budgets beyond hosted limits. Self-hosted runners remain a future extension.
Retry infrastructure failures at most once on a fresh runner and retain the first attempt. Never rescore normal failures or agent timeouts. Lost receipts mean unknown spend, not free execution.

planSections.title: Cost and usage
paragraphs: Reported cost → LiteLLM completion_cost → official pricing snapshot × token usage. Use Unknown only when required data is still missing. ACP carries cache counters and completeness; context occupancy is not billing usage.

Request cost = [(input − cached) × input rate + cached × cache rate + output × output rate] / 1,000,000. Do not add reasoning tokens again when already included in output. Sum permitted attempts per task and weight benchmark costs equally.

Missing cache detail uses an uncached upper bound. DeepSeek uses peak-rate bounds when billing-time detail is absent. Mark these estimates and exclude them from the deterministic Pareto frontier. Freeze prices and FX; distinguish estimates from billed charges. Track tool, judge, and runner costs separately; missing is not zero.

planSections.title: Public archives and private comparisons
paragraphs: Public runs contain QwenPaw only. Private comparisons group by model × harness × SDK. Codex, Claude Code, and DeepSeek Harness demos do not imply verified integrations. Private results stay in private deployments and never enter the public bundle.

Validate allowlisted fields, coverage, and visibility, then archive immutable runs on the bench-results branch by manifest identity. Serialize index updates, make repeat publication idempotent, and reject conflicting rewrites. Every website build reads the same history.

Model jobs receive only the Bench model secret and have no publishing permission. Publishing jobs receive no model key. Export structured statistics only; raw requests and unredacted traces are not automatically public. Demos have no fabricated evidence links.

planSections.title: Offline parity and acceptance
paragraphs: Fix task sets, models, tools, budgets, and graders. Document official-condition replication separately from controlled comparisons. Reports identify applicable SHAs and known differences; releases reference offline reports without online confirmation.

Official publication requires resource and protocol acceptance plus complete benchmark runs. Keep implemented code, mock layouts, and measured results distinct. Single-task smoke checks are not official benchmark scores.
